perf.summary: Replace the double modulo ((a % p) + p) % p with one modulo plus a branchless/conditional add.
perf.currentCost: Two integer divisions per call (a % p, then (...) % p). For positive a already < p this still pays two divides; the second % p is only needed because a%p in C# can be negative.
perf.proposedChange: a %= p; if (a < 0) a += p;  (single division). This matches the normalization already used inside ModPow.Run.
perf.rationale: a % p is in (-p, p); adding p once when negative yields the canonical residue in [0,p). One divide instead of two removes a ~20-40 cycle op. The subsequent a==0 test and ModPow exponent are unchanged.
perf.risk: Behavior identical for all valid p>0. (If p could be <=0 the function was already undefined.) No overflow: a + p stays within long since a in (-p,0).

perf.summary: Remove the redundant private ModPow wrapper and the unused 'using System'.
perf.currentCost: A private static long ModPow merely forwards to IAFahim.Math.NT.ModPow.Run; it adds an extra named indirection and a name collision risk. 'using System;' is unused.
perf.proposedChange: Delete the wrapper and call ModPow.Run (or fully-qualified IAFahim.Math.NT.ModPow.Run) directly at the call site; drop using System.
perf.rationale: Fewer symbols, clearer call graph, no dead using. ModPow.Run is already AggressiveInlining so there is no perf reason for the wrapper; it only obscures.
perf.risk: None functionally. Purely cosmetic/discoverability; verify no other member references the local ModPow (it does not).

perf.summary: Branchless final result selection from the ModPow value.
perf.currentCost: if (val == p - 1) return -1; return 1; is a predictable-but-present branch.
perf.proposedChange: long pm1 = p - 1; return (val == pm1) ? -1 : 1;  or branchless: return 1 - (int)((val == pm1) ? 2 : 0). Also reuse pm1 for the exponent (p-1)>>1.
perf.rationale: Computing p-1 once and reusing it for both the exponent shift and the comparison removes a duplicate subtraction; a ternary compiles to a conditional move under Burst, avoiding a branch misprediction on inputs where the quadratic residue split is ~50/50.
perf.risk: None; same outputs. The val==0 case cannot occur here because a!=0 mod prime p implies val in {1, p-1}.
